IncidentBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED — elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (us-west1)

IncidentBot: Summary: traffic spike + cache invalidation storm causing backend pool to fall back to cold model loads -> sustained 503/504s for approx 3.5m. Pager sent to @oncall.

Alice Rivera: I'm oncall. I'm seeing ~18% 5xx for the last 4m, latency spiking to ~4.2s p95. Rolling metrics:
```
region: us-west1
endpoint: /v1/generate
error_rate: 18% -> 22% over 3m
primary_model_pool: rdx-medium-1
fallback_pool: rdx-medium-1-quantized
```
Alice Rivera: Paging SRE and runtime team. I'll assemble current mitigation steps.

Samir Patel: On it. First guess: the prefix/KV cache invalidation TTL bump yesterday + a race in our cache warm-up caused N cold starts. Looking at logs:
```
2026-03-12T14:22:11Z rdx-runtime[pid=8219] WARN kvcache: miss key=conv:abc123
2026-03-12T14:22:12Z rdx-runtime[pid=8219] INFO model_loader: start load rdx-medium-1 (cold)
2026-03-12T14:22:13Z rdx-runtime[pid=8219] ERROR http: upstream read timeout
```
Samir Patel: Immediate mitigation I recommend: 1) Temporarily route traffic off us-west1 primary pool to dedicated warm pool in us-west2, 2) Increase cache TTL rollback to previous safe value, 3) Enable fast-fallback to quantized variant for requests >2s latency.

Maya Chen: I can push the routing change and fast-fallback now. Will also check kernel load on the GPUs.

Priya Kaur: Heads-up for Support: customers are starting tickets saying "API returning 503s". Need a short customer macro and status page copy. I can draft.

Alice Rivera: Action list (live):
- [x] acknowledge incident (IncidentBot)
- [x] page SRE/Runtime (Samir/Maya)
- [ ] route traffic to warm pool (Maya)
- [ ] rollback TTL change (Samir)
- [ ] post interim status (Priya)
- [ ] prepare CS macro and Zendesk reply (Ben/Priya)
- [ ] monitor metrics for stabilization (Alice)

Samir Patel: Rolling TTL rollback now (config change):
```
PATCH /internal/config/cache
{"kv_ttl_ms": 86400000, "note":"rollback pre-2026-03-12"}
```
Samir Patel: TTL rollback accepted. Triggering warm pool routing.

Maya Chen: Routing change executed: sent 25% of new requests to us-west2 warm pool, 75% still to us-west1 primary while we verify. Command used:
```
rdxctl route set --from us-west1 --to us-west2 --percent 25 --route-policy fast-warm
```
Maya Chen: Also enabled fast-fallback to quantized model variant for requests exceeding 1.8s p95.

Alice Rivera: Metrics check 2m after changes: error rate down to 7.2%, p95 latency 1.5s, errors trending down. Good sign.

Priya Kaur: Drafting public status page entry and short Zendesk/Intercom macros below. Please review and approve quickly so Support can respond.

Priya Kaur: STATUS PAGE (short):
"We're investigating elevated errors for text generation in the US-West region. Some customers may see 5xx responses and higher latencies. Mitigation is in progress; we will provide updates every 15 minutes until resolved."

Priya Kaur: STATUS PAGE (detailed for post-mortem update):
"At 14:22 UTC we observed a sudden increase in 5xx responses for /v1/generate in us-west1. Root cause: a cache invalidation TTL change combined with a cache warm-up race causing excessive cold model loads and upstream timeouts. Mitigation: rolled back TTL, routed a portion of traffic to a warm pool in us-west2, and enabled fast-fallback to quantized model variants. Services are recovering; a full post-mortem will follow once metrics stabilize."

Priya Kaur: SUPPORT MACROS — Zendesk quick reply (concise):
"Hi {{customer.first_name}},

Thanks for flagging this. We’re seeing elevated 5xx responses for text generation in the US-West region and have active mitigations in place (traffic reroute and cache rollback). You should see reduced errors shortly. We’ll follow up with a full incident summary once service is stable. If you need an SLA credit request, reply to this thread and we’ll escalate.

— Priya (Redwood Support)"

Priya Kaur: SUPPORT MACROS — Intercom short reply (chat):
"Hi there — quick update: we're aware of errors affecting text generation in US-West. Our engineering team has applied mitigations; performance is improving. Apologies for the disruption. I’ll notify you when we’ve fully resolved it."

Priya Kaur: SUPPORT CHECKLIST FOR AGENTS (copyable):
1) Confirm customer's region (if using regional endpoints).
2) Offer the Zendesk macro above.
3) If customer reports persistent errors >10m after mitigation, escalate to Level 2 with ticket tag "incident-usw-gen".
4) Collect request_id (if provided), sample payloads, and timestamps.
5) Offer temporary workarounds: retry logic with exponential backoff or alternate region endpoints (us-east1/us-west2) if latency allows.

Ben O'Neill: Approved. Small tweak: in macro add sentence about alternate endpoints: "You can temporarily target us-west2 or us-east1 while we finish remediation." Other than that, good.

Maya Chen: Systems report: GPU load normalized after routing; memory pressure reduced on primary pool. Still watching KV cache hit ratio.

Samir Patel: Monitoring: error rate now <3% and holding. I’ll keep TTL rollback in place until tomorrow 02:00 UTC, then we can safe-roll forward after additional warm-up automation is in place.

Alice Rivera: Oncall handoff note (for next shift):
- Incident: elevated 5xx on /v1/generate us-west1 due to cache TTL + warm-up race.
- Mitigations applied: TTL rollback, partial routing to warm pool (us-west2), fast-fallback to quantized model variants.
- Current state: stabilized, error rate <3%, monitoring.
- Followups: implement automated staggered cache invalidation and warm-up, update runbook, add traffic ramp playbook.

Ben O'Neill: I'll send an outbound customer email template once postmortem draft is ready. Draft below for review: 
"Subject: Incident: Text generation errors in US-West (Resolved)

Hi {{account_admin}},

We experienced elevated errors affecting text generation in the US-West region earlier today. Our engineers mitigated the issue by rolling back a cache TTL change and routing traffic to a warm pool; services are now stable. We're preparing a post-incident report that will include root cause and steps we will take to prevent recurrence.

We apologize for the disruption. If you experienced any business impact and would like to discuss SLA credits, reply to this message and we’ll prioritize your request.

— Redwood Inference Support Team"

Alice Rivera: Good. I’ll leave a short incident summary in the incident channel and create a postmortem ticket. Thanks everyone for the fast response. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: Incident marked "mitigated" by Alice Rivera at 14:34 UTC. Postmortem ticket created: PM-3445.

Priya Kaur: I'll update the status page with the "mitigated" state and post the more detailed explanation after the postmortem.

Samir Patel: Leaving a note to automation/content teams: add a pre-approved macro set for oncall to reduce Support friction. Tagging @devex for follow-up.

Maya Chen: +1 on automation. I'll open a runtime PR to add warm-up handshake before TTL changes.

Ben O'Neill: Closing customer-facing comms loop: once postmortem is ready I'll send the email to impacted accounts list.

Alice Rivera: Thread closed for now. If anything regresses, re-open and we re-page.
